column1: How Wiederhold's sketch of Trenton was tied to the current street map

The sketch is not a survey. Six places in the town centre were matched to the same places on the current street map (OpenStreetMap, S39) and a best-fit shift, turn and uniform scale computed from them: 0.689 m per pixel, turned 4.4 degrees.

The fit holds from the English Church south to the creek and east to the surrender ground. North of the church the sketch is squeezed to about half scale, and the outposts are not to scale, so positions there come from markers, street corners or distances scaled along a road.

How Mouzon's map of 1775 (S135) was laid on the ground for the South Carolina reconstruction (pipeline/georef/sc_mouzon_fit.py, sc_mouzon_fit.json)

The Library of Congress copy is cut into sections and mounted on cloth. Each section (above and below the gap at crop y 1222, left and right of the seam at crop x 4232) is fitted by a thin-plate spline with a plane, from the point controls below and from Mouzon's rivers, coast and North Carolina line matched seven times over to the same lines in Natural Earth (S136). Pixels are of the half-resolution crop: full scan x = 2 x, y = 3600 + 2 y. Misfit is the distance at which a control is found when it is left out of the fit.
